reasons: Governing law in Section 15.5 (p0627) is expressly the laws of the State of New York with conflicts rules disclaimed, which matches the rule's preferred jurisdiction exactly; the deterministic check on the accepted law set also passes.

The dispute forum is not walk-away territory: arbitration is administered by JAMS (a US administrator) under its Comprehensive Rules, awards are enforceable in 'any court having jurisdiction' (p0630), IP scope/validity/infringement disputes go to courts (p0637), and either Party retains court access for interim and equitable relief (p0639). There is no exclusive foreign venue and no identified foreign arbitral seat.

Election of domestic arbitration rather than exclusive New York County court jurisdiction is a sub-element short of the preferred wording, correctly noted in the rationale rather than redlined under the playbook's classification semantics.

The rationale appropriately flags the redacted seat/arbitrator count as a diligence item and states that a foreign seat would convert the finding to a deviation, so the compliant call is properly qualified.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment was proposed; the rendered text is unchanged from the originals, so there is no risk of an over-flag or invalid edit.
